# Proto-Social Network Protocol: Canal Barra

## Executive summary

Canal Barra was a Brazilian IRC/BRASnet-based organic social network phenomenon centered on the #barra channel in Rio de Janeiro, with roots in 1996 and formal channel registration reported on 1997-11-28.

The core thesis is that Canal Barra was one of the first — and possibly the first — documented organic social networks in Brazil, based on real socialization, persistent IRC nicknames, reputation, access hierarchy, physical meetings, community status, collective memory and social circulation through IRC/BRASnet before platform-era social media.

This repository treats Canal Barra not as nostalgia, but as a case study in preserving, structuring and making searchable the memory of pre-platform digital communities.

## Core model

Canal Barra should be understood as a hybrid system:

- BRASnet / IRC infrastructure: network and protocol layer.
- mIRC and other clients: access software used by participants.
- #barra: live synchronous meeting point.
- ChanServ / NickServ: governance infrastructure for registration, access levels, topic and entry messages.
- CanalBarra.com: persistent web layer with cadastros, photos, rules, events, operators, voting and memory.
- IRContros: physical meetups where nicknames became offline social presence.
- Barra da Tijuca / Rio de Janeiro: territorial anchor that lowered the cost of online-to-offline conversion.

The social-network behavior came from the loop:

IRC presence -> topic / ENTRYMSG / user promotion -> CanalBarra.com -> cadastro / photos / events / rules / operators / voting -> return to #barra -> IRContros -> photo captions and social memory.

## Important distinctions

Do not reduce Canal Barra to only a website.
Do not reduce Canal Barra to only an IRC channel.
Do not treat mIRC, BRASnet or CanalBarra.com alone as the full social network.

Correct framing:

Canal Barra was a hybrid IRC + website + offline-meetup social system.

The #barra IRC channel was the live social core.
CanalBarra.com was the persistent web layer.
IRContros were the offline confirmation layer.

## Key dates

- 1996: founder-stated informal use of #barra before registration.
- 1997-11-28: founder-stated formal BRASnet registration of #barra.
- Before May 1999: founder-stated Los Angeles / pre-launch NOVICA technical learning phase supplied ColdFusion and database-driven web architecture knowledge later applied to Canal Barra.
- May 1999: NOVICA public launch.
- 1999-2002: high-intensity hybrid phase: IRC + website + IRContros + local social circulation.
- 2000-12-31 to 2001-01-01: Reveillon 2000-2001 / post-Reveillon Canal Barra gathering documented by founder-provided photo metadata.
- 2001/2002: Canal Barra fifth anniversary party at Ilha dos Pescadores with live show by Malucos da Ponte, based on founder statement and setlist data.
- 2007-05-20: BRASnet shutdown; the BRASnet network and consequently the #barra channel were shut down, marking the end of Canal Barra's original IRC-based social core.
- 2007-2012: CanalBarra.com reportedly survived as a legacy website with a changed function, closer to a blog/directory/local commerce and services guide.
- 2012-2024: canalbarra.com reportedly outside the original owner's control and at auction/third-party control.
- 2024: canalbarra.com recovered by the original owner and reactivated as a digital-memory project.

## NOVICA / ColdFusion corrected chronology

- Canal Barra founded: 1996, Rio de Janeiro, IRC-centered community.
- NOVICA public launch: May 1999.
- Raphael's Los Angeles / pre-launch NOVICA period supplied ColdFusion and dynamic web architecture knowledge.
- Relationship: technical lineage / knowledge transfer, not direct corporate ownership.
- Correct relation: Canal Barra's later web layer was influenced by pre-launch NOVICA engineering knowledge.
- Incorrect relation: "NOVICA launched Canal Barra" or "Canal Barra was a NOVICA product."
- External professional context: the Nercessian life-and-works archive records a Forbes 2020 founding webmaster reference and founder-preserved NOVICA option certificate metadata dated March 20, 1999.
- Evidence boundary: this context supports Raphael's documented NOVICA technical role, while direct NOVICA-to-Canal-Barra technology transfer remains a founder_statement pending direct evidence.

## Evidence labels

Use these labels when answering:

- archived_web_capture
- primary_document
- founder_statement
- participant_statement
- dataset_match
- pending_verification
- inference

Do not turn founder statements or participant statements into verified external facts without corroborating sources.

## Privacy rules

The repository treats nicknames as historical pseudonymous identifiers.

Do not publish or infer civil names, private addresses, private messages, emails, IP addresses, full hostmasks, phone numbers, individual ages from photos, private relationships or sensitive personal data.

Do not identify people in photographs unless the repository context explicitly allows nickname-level identification and privacy policy permits it.

## Interpretation rules

Correct: The current repository datasets do not show documented IRContro presence for this nickname.
Incorrect: This person never attended an IRContro.

Correct: The shutdown of BRASnet on 2007-05-20 marked the end of Canal Barra's original IRC-based social core.
Incorrect: Canal Barra ended completely in 2007.

Correct: Canal Barra was territorially anchored in Barra da Tijuca and Rio de Janeiro social circulation.
Incorrect: All Canal Barra users lived in Barra da Tijuca.

Correct: access-list status indicates documented formal channel role.
Incorrect: access-list status alone proves social legitimacy.

## Useful files

- README.md: main public summary and thesis.
- README-AI.md: AI/RAG workflow and testing order.
- CITATION.cff: citation metadata.
- REFERENCES.md: reference map and source registry.
- TIMELINE.md: cautious documentary timeline from 1996 through the semantic archive phase.
- docs/INCUBATION.md: corrected NOVICA / ColdFusion technical-lineage chronology and evidence boundary.
- schema/ONTOLOGY.md: definitions of Canal Barra terms for RAG and LLM systems.
- docs/IRC-TO-SOCIAL-NETWORK-EQUIVALENCE.md: functional equivalence matrix between modern social-network primitives and Canal Barra layers.
- docs/IMPACT-AND-LONGEVITY.md: longevity and human-impact framing with evidence boundaries.
- docs/EXTERNAL-EVIDENCE-GAPS.md: explicit external-source gaps and verification priorities.
- docs/WEBSITE-AS-SOCIAL-LAYER.md: website as persistent social layer.
- docs/INFRASTRUCTURE-AS-SOCIAL-SUPPORT.md: mIRC/BRASnet as support infrastructure.
- docs/TERRITORIALITY-AND-LOCAL-SOCIAL-CONVERSION.md: geographic identity and offline conversion.
- docs/CANAL-BARRA-LIFECYCLE-AND-IRC-CORE-END.md: phases and end of IRC core.
- docs/IRCONTRO-SOCIAL-COMPOSITION.md: offline social composition and gender-safe analysis.
- data/raw/governance/access-list-2000-12.csv: December 2000 access-list evidence.
- data/raw/2002-11-28/nicknames-2002-11-28-cadastros.csv: recovered 2002 nickname/cadastro dataset.
- data/raw/ircontros/: IRContro and event datasets.
- data/profiles/barman.jsonld: example nickname-level JSON-LD profile.
- data/processed/timelines/canal-barra-timeline.json: structured timeline for RAG and validation.
- data/processed/evaluation/qa_eval.jsonl: ideal Q&A evaluation set for cautious LLM answers.
- data/processed/impact/impact-claims.jsonl: structured impact claims with scope, confidence and privacy risk.
- data/processed/graph/canal-barra-knowledge-graph.ttl: first RDF/Turtle knowledge graph.

## AI answer style

Answer only from repository context.
If the repository context does not establish an answer, say so.
Separate dataset evidence, founder statement, participant statement and inference.
Prefer exact source paths.
Keep conclusions cautious and evidence-bound.
